clue.text: Drama teacher's outmoded form of transport

parts.note: the stage is shorthand for theatre and drama as a profession
a coach is a trainer or tutor; the possessive simply joins the two parts

explanation.surface: A drama teacher gets about by some old-fashioned means of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse-drawn carriages carrying passengers on fixed routes were superseded by railways and motor vehicles, so they are now obsolete.

clue.text: Latin American dance some vassals attempted

indicators.note: 'some' means only a portion of the following words is taken, a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Feudal servants try their feet at a lively Latin dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively partner dance originated in Cuba and Puerto Rican communities of New York, set to Caribbean rhythms.

clue.text: A nice gal's unconventional painkiller

indicators.note: something unconventional departs from the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: all nine letters, including the S of the possessive, are the fodder

explanation.surface: A pleasant young woman has an odd remedy for pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesics are drugs such as aspirin or paracetamol that relieve aches without causing unconsciousness.

clue.text: Young swimmer always seen around lake

indicators.note: one word is seen surrounding another, so it wraps around the next piece

parts.note: ever means at all times
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A youthful swimmer is forever spotted circling a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvers are juvenile eels that migrate upriver from the sea, so they are fish in an early stage of life.

clue.text: Rower principally operating on a river

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' places one part directly above the next part
principally points to the chief or leading part of the word before it, its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of operating
taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone rowing is mainly working out on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The blade that propels a boat does the rowing, so the implement can loosely be called a rower; it also means an oarsman.

clue.text: WWII ally using Asian language in court?

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it, wrapped by the outer letters

parts.note: CT is a standard abbreviation for court
Hindi is a principal language of India

explanation.surface: A wartime partner speaks an Asian language in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chindits were British and Indian special forces fighting behind Japanese lines in Burma; the question mark flags the unusual definition.
explanation.definitionFit: These long-range jungle troops fought on the Allied side against Japan in Burma during the Second World War.

clue.text: Friend in French department — Hannah, possibly

parts.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written
the Drôme is a département in south-east France

explanation.surface: A friend lives in a French region, perhaps called Hannah.
explanation.walkthrough: Hannah reads the same backwards and forwards; 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A word spelt identically from either end is an example of the category, and this name is a classic instance.

clue.text: Everyone originally occupying a town in Clackmannanshire

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

parts.note: the first letter of occupying
taken as written

explanation.surface: Everybody first moved into a small Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Clackmannanshire is the smallest historic county of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is the administrative centre of that Scottish county, on the north bank of the Forth estuary.

clue.text: Disappear, carrying right sort of coating

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it within, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to vanish is to disappear

explanation.surface: Something vanishes while taking the correct kind of finish.

clue.text: Cheer pilot manoeuvring hovering aircraft

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving things into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: all ten letters of the two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Applaud the pilot steering a craft that hangs in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotor-driven machines can stay stationary in mid-air, unlike fixed-wing planes, which is their defining ability.

clue.text: Speech made in summer month by Russian river

parts.note: taken as written
AUG is the calendar abbreviation for August
the Ural flows from Russia through Kazakhstan to the Caspian

explanation.surface: An address delivered in midsummer beside a river in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, chiefly American, the word names the first formal address given by someone taking office.

clue.text: Most foolish American, anyway!

second meaning: a North American informal adverb meaning at any rate

explanation.surface: Someone declares an American the silliest, at any rate!
explanation.definitionFit: In US informal speech the single word serves as a sentence adverb meaning at least, in any case.

clue.text: Split grain young chap brought from east

explanation.definitionFit: Dal is dried pulses such as lentils that have been hulled and halved, a staple of South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Scandinavian course a Norwegian ultimately enters

taken as written

parts.note: the last letter of Norwegian

explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is one of the Nordic nations, so a person or thing from there belongs to Scandinavia.

clue.text: VIP absorbing atmosphere at first in African capital

indicators.note: something absorbing another takes it in, so one word holds the next

parts.note: a nob is an informal British term for a wealthy or important person
air means atmosphere

indicators.note: at first means at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the following word counts

parts.note: the first letter of in

explanation.surface: A dignitary breathes in the atmosphere on first arriving in an African capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital and largest city of Kenya, in East Africa.

clue.text: Emcee securing sparkling wine and aromatic resin

explanation.surface: A master of ceremonies grabs some fizz and a fragrant gum.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a gum exuded by a Mediterranean shrub, used in varnishes and to flavour food and drink.

clue.text: Broad sash initially introduced by former pupil

parts.note: the first letter of introduced

explanation.surface: An old student first brought in a wide sash.

clue.text: Leader of heathen sect paid out for military recruit's position

the letters of these two words join the anagram

clue.text: Line up something to wear

second meaning: a one-piece garment for women and girls

clue.text: Entertainers — lots of them!

clue.text: European design producing strong feeling

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

clue.text: Mischievous type of politician supporting India

parts.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

clue.text: Children? That's the problem

explanation.surface: A weary parent sighs that kids are the trouble.

clue.text: Oust police officer's back-up group primarily serving sheriff

parts.note: the first letter of serving
the first letter of sheriff

explanation.surface: A detective's reinforcements, led by a sheriff, eject someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispossess is to deprive someone of property or position, effectively expelling or evicting them.
